evidence.quote: Let 𝒟 = { ( x i , y i ) } i = 1 n \mathcal{D}=\{(x_{i},y_{i})\}_{i=1}^{n} be an offline training set, let f f be a frozen language model, and let c ∈ 𝒞 c\in\mathcal{C} denote textual context supplied alongside an input. We define the empirical context risk as
We then perform a deterministic breadth-first traversal from those entries, expanding neighbors in order of learned edge utility, under fixed hop, node, and token budgets.

Helpful and harmful labels contribute confidence-weighted evidence to the corresponding edges, while neutral labels leave the counters unchanged. The traversal utility is the mean of the resulting Beta posterior, so retrieval preferentially follows transitions with stronger helpful evidence.

The difference appears during curation: the Curator produces a graph update that may add or revise bullet-point nodes, add or revise edges, or do both. The update is applied locally without rewriting the rest of the graph.

Only after producing y ^ t \widehat{y}_{t} does the Reflector inspect the prediction, available feedback, and execution trace. The Curator then emits local graph edits, which are applied to obtain G ( t + 1 ) G^{(t+1)} . Consequently, information derived from y t y_{t} cannot affect the prediction on x t x_{t} ; it becomes available only to subsequent examples. The Generator and Reflector retain ACE’s core roles, with the additional memory-use tracing and edge feedback described above, while the Retriever and graph-valued Curator implement the two GraphMemory-specific interfaces described in Section 3 .

Each system processes the training split for one epoch, and the then-current memory is evaluated on the validation split every 100 updates. The checkpoint with the highest validation accuracy is selected for the held-out test evaluation.

GraphMemory learns relations between strategies from confidence-weighted helpful and harmful feedback, supporting their composition without requiring predefined edge types or training a retrieval policy.

The retrieval weight is a smoothed estimate of how often the Reflector has judged an observed directed transition helpful under the current retrieval policy. It should not be interpreted as a causal measure of interaction between two nodes or as a calibrated probability that retrieving the edge will improve accuracy. Evidence is policy-dependent because highly ranked edges are more likely to be observed again, and ranking by the posterior mean does not explicitly reward uncertainty. These limitations are important when interpreting the learned graph.
Qwen costs are API-equivalent estimates; the experiments ran locally using a quantized model.

ACE/Qwen3.8-27B on FiNER exceeded the 48 GB memory available on our local hardware (RTX 6000) as its full-memory context grew, even with 4-bit quantization. This highlights a practical limitation of ACE’s context growth. This is preliminary workshop work, we leave a hardware-matched run to future evaluation.
The bounded-retrieval result in Proposition 2 applies to the serialized node content supplied to the Generator. It does not include the compact index read by the Retriever.

Our results remain preliminary, covering two related tasks, two models, and one primary baseline. Broader evaluations, additional memory and prompt-optimization baselines, and repeated runs are needed.

evidence.quote: The model supplies a set of input points together with their spatial relations, and the harness automatically solves and executes the corresponding action. The model must distinguish between on-hand and off-hand points: on-hand points lie on the gripper or on a held object and their positions can be modified, whereas off-hand points are fixed in the scene. The harness drives the on-hand points so that they satisfy the spatial constraints specified by the model through the following pipeline:

To refine robot action or to improve robustness when the constraints fail (for example, when the object slips out of the gripper), we also expose direct low-level robot control interfaces. These interfaces share the same coordinate frame defined in Section 3.1.1 , so that the LLM can interpret and use them consistently.
The prompt is specific to each task but shared across instances, and is written by a human.

To mitigate this on BEHAVIOR long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks, we hand-craft a task-specific prompt for every task that specifies the execution steps and the behavioral boundaries the model must respect.
Future work aims to close this gap further by training the model or evolving the harness to become more physically grounded.
We distill the procedures used across individual tasks into a set of reusable embodied skills, listed in Table 6 .

Generative AI tools were used in three ways. (i) They assisted writing. (ii) They assisted running the experiments: launching jobs, monitoring long rollouts, and flagging failed runs so that each experiment kept running stably, while every experimental setting and every reported number was checked by the authors. (iii) They assisted coding: writing and debugging RoboHarness human interface.
